message.content:
To terminate **Visual Studio Code** (the `code.exe` process) from the command line on Windows, you can use the built‑in `taskkill` utility.

### Basic command

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM` – specifies the image name (`code.exe`)  
* `/F` – forces termination (equivalent to “kill”)

This will immediately stop *all* running instances of `code.exe`.

---

### If you only want to kill a specific instance

1. Find the PID(s) of the VS Code processes:

   ```cmd
   tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
   ```

2. Kill the desired one:

   ```cmd
   taskkill /PID <PID_NUMBER> /F
   ```

Replace `<PID_NUMBER>` with the actual Process ID shown in the list.

---

### Notes & Tips

| What | Why |
|------|-----|
| Run CMD as Administrator | Some processes may require elevated rights to be terminated. |
| Use `/T` flag | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` also terminates child processes spawned by VS Code. |
| Verify before killing | `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"` lets you confirm which instances exist. |

That’s it—just paste the appropriate command into a Command Prompt window and hit Enter.
